card.intuition: Progressive disclosure means loading only the context an agent needs right now, with context pointers to the rest. It inverts the always-loaded AGENTS.md mindset because every token loaded up front is billed and spends attention on every turn.
card.analogy: An IDE that shows only the toolbar relevant to the file you are editing and hides the rest behind a click, instead of dumping every menu onto the screen at once.
card.time_complexity: O(context actually needed per turn): by keeping the always-loaded layer small, a sentence per topic plus a pointer, most tokens are never loaded, reducing per-turn input cost.
card.space_complexity: O(one-line pointers): the always-loaded layer holds pointers, not bodies, so the finite context window stays small and the detail loads only when triggered.
when_to_use: When an AGENTS.md stuffed with a full style guide, deploy runbook, and database conventions is making the model worse at all of them
When the tell is an agent that ignores rules you know are in its context because they are buried
When you want the agent to read the style guide only while writing a component, or the runbook only while deploying
When using skills, the pattern built into the harness, whose full instructions load only when triggered
gotchas: Context is a cost twice over — every token is billed as input and spends attention budget even when unneeded
A pointer that is too vague gives the agent no reason to follow it and the detail never loads
Instructions that genuinely apply to every task should stay inline, not be hidden behind disclosure

steps.label: Pointer
steps.annotation: The always-loaded layer holds a short sentence per topic plus a context pointer to where the detail lives.

steps.label: Match
steps.annotation: When the current task matches, the agent recognizes the description and decides the detail is worth loading.

steps.label: Load
steps.annotation: The agent follows the pointer and pulls the full instructions into the context window.

steps.label: Drop
steps.annotation: Once the task is done the detail leaves context and stops spending tokens or attention.

exercise.prompt: Write a function that stores a topic inline when it applies every turn and as a pointer otherwise. Both branches return a label prefixed to the topic.
hints: The always-loaded layer inlines only rules that apply every turn
Anything else should be a pointer so it loads on demand
exercise.test_code:
assert plan('test command', True) == 'inline:test command'
assert plan('style guide', False) == 'pointer:style guide'
print('PASS')
